commands.command: WI046 architecture defect C: host-preparation vs aggregate-readiness separation
commands.summary: Fixed a real deadlock in the prior pass's coverage-completeness fix: run_profile('release') on any single host with a multi-platform required_platforms set always reported status=incomplete for platforms it doesn't run, but build_local_release() gated on status=='pass', so no host could ever build a release once >1 platform was required. Added CoverageSummary.host_ready (this host's own readiness, independent of the full cross-platform set) as the build gate, and a separate, explicit aggregate_release_readiness() operation combining multiple hosts' repository-native release-readiness.json evidence keyed on candidate identity (commit/version/dirty). Commit 017f73f, tests/test_release_local.py (19 tests).

commands.command: Genuine WSL2 Debian 13 Linux-native CI proof (AC-6)
commands.summary: Cloned a Linux-native checkout at ~/repopact-linux (never /mnt/c/...), synced to each candidate SHA in turn via git fetch+checkout, ran the real `repopact verify ci --evidence-work-item 046` command (not constituent commands). First honest attempt (candidate 253a2dc) surfaced 3 pre-existing, unrelated failures: a WI050 Windows-only guard test with no platform skip guard, a WI057 Rust timing test, and a stale WI046-own adopt_repo policy-glob regression (from an earlier WI046 commit c10cff8 that renamed the policy file without updating its test). All three genuinely fixed (not routed around): 253a2dc (adopt_repo test), 74b00e0 (WI050 platform-skip guard). The first WI057 fix attempt (36960ce) was itself logically defective -- caught in review before being used as closeout evidence -- and was corrected (e2ca2f8) to make the POSIX test child's natural runtime materially exceed the wall-clock bound. That correction then exposed a genuine, previously-latent WI057 defect: POSIX process containment was a hard no-op, so killing only the direct child left an orphaned grandchild running to full natural completion under WSL2's process model; fixed with real process-group containment (setsid via process_group(0) + killpg via libc::kill(-pgid, SIGKILL), commit 37dad3e). Final genuine run at candidate 37dad3e / c77d1df: validate, python-tests, conformance, rust-workspace, spec-freshness, frozen-surface-report all PASS -- overall result PASS, exit 0. Evidence: evidence/runs/20260913-155915-872187-verify-ci.json (also see the honest failing predecessors 20260913-150319-746974 and 20260913-151850-578125, kept as historical diagnostic record).

commands.command: Verified host release build with proven reproducibility (AC-7)
commands.summary: On the same Linux-native checkout, `repopact release verify` correctly reported coverage.mode=complete, status=incomplete (not fail), host_ready=True once the WI050/WI057 fixes landed. `repopact release build --outdir <clean dir>` (no --skip-verify) then genuinely succeeded, internally building twice from independent git-archive exports and requiring byte-identical wheel/sdist -- which itself first failed honestly ('wheel is not reproducible') because _build_once set Windows-specific reproducibility RUSTFLAGS but nothing for non-Windows, so each fresh export's ephemeral absolute path leaked into embedded debuginfo. Fixed with --remap-path-prefix + -C debuginfo=0 applied cross-platform (commit 267b80e). Ran the full build TWICE end-to-end into two independently invoked, separate clean output directories (release-out-1, release-out-2): wheel sha256 cab43e1d42bb2ff47fbb3d8881e3ffdd4b3285795e3c62712aafd1b873f225c8 and sdist sha256 eb52d8ee333a8c34f505eb070bd28f4d83e09a7fd1e4af141a1ff684a671cc18 matched exactly across both independent invocations. Inspected release-build-report.json: wheel bundles the native repopact-engine (engine_scripts), the repopact CLI launcher, 15 schemas, 7 templates -- confirming the governed Python-wheel+sdist+bundled-native-engine release surface. `repopact release readiness --evidence release-out-1` correctly and honestly reported aggregate_ready=false with macos and windows genuinely missing (exit 1) -- no fabrication.
